## What it is

Spanish-language dance music from Puerto Rico and Panama, built on the **dembow**: the kick on every beat,
and the snare on the last sixteenth of beat 1 and the and of 2 (and again in beats 3 and 4), a 3+3+2 in
sixteenths over each half bar, under long synth chords and a rapped or sung vocal.

## A little history

The rhythm is named after Shabba Ranks' Jamaican dancehall record *Dem Bow* (1990), whose riddim (the
backing track, by Steely & Clevie, built on their *Poco Man Jam*) was copied everywhere. In Panama,
artists such as El General sang Spanish lyrics over dancehall riddims (*reggae en español*). In Puerto Rico
in the 1990s DJ Playero and others made underground mixtapes on the same beats; the name *reggaeton* took
hold around the turn of the century. Daddy Yankee's *Gasolina* (2004) was the international breakthrough,
Luis Fonsi and Daddy Yankee's *Despacito* (2017) one of the most-streamed songs ever, and Bad Bunny the
genre's biggest star of the 2020s.

## The band's version

- **Bass:** *3+3+2 (tresillo)*. **Comping:** long held chords. **Drums:** dembow.

## Listening

| Recording | Year | Listen for |
|---|---|---|
| Shabba Ranks, *Dem Bow* | 1990 | The record the rhythm is named after. |
| El General, *Te Ves Buena* | 1991 | Reggae en español from Panama. |
| Daddy Yankee, *Gasolina* | 2004 | The breakthrough. |
| Luis Fonsi ft. Daddy Yankee, *Despacito* | 2017 | Dembow under a pop song. |
| Bad Bunny, *Tití Me Preguntó* | 2022 | The current sound. |

### More recent

| Recording | Year | Listen for |
|---|---|---|
| Karol G & Nicki Minaj, *Tusa* | 2019 | Dembow under a pop-ballad chord loop. |
